title: 1990 AHSME Problem 22
statement: If the six solutions of \(x^6=-64\) are written in the form \(a+bi,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are real, then the product of those solutions with \(a\gt0\) is

solutions.text:
The roots have modulus \(2\) and arguments \[ \frac\pi6+\frac{k\pi}{3},\qquad k=0,1,\ldots,5. \] The roots with positive real part have arguments \(\frac{\pi}{6}\) and \(\frac{11\pi}{6}.\) They are conjugates of modulus \(2,\) so their product is \(2^2=4.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
